name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,207

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scientist’s ending last letter to say further brain measurements will reveal pious people

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word scientist
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
to add is to say something more
IQ scores measure intelligence

explanation.surface: A scientist's closing remark promises that more brain scans will expose the devout.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare Hebrew loanword: build it piece by piece and trust the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tzaddiqs are righteous holy men in Jewish tradition, so the plural fits devout believers.

clue.text: Gum resins inflamed asthma besetting Bill on two occasions

indicators.note: something inflamed is agitated, so these letters are stirred up
besetting means surrounding on all sides

blocks.note: taken as written
AC, account, a bill, written twice

explanation.surface: Resinous gums aggravate asthma, troubling Bill twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ACs are placed among the jumbled letters; the order of operations matters less than the letter count.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacamahac is an aromatic resin from certain poplars and tropical trees, used in ointments.

clue.text: Computer algorithms run voice

blocks.note: artificial intelligence
R for run, in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Software routines operate speech recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: To air an opinion is to voice it, both verbs meaning express openly.

clue.text: Put Indian bread into sauce, say, wrapping old type of fish

indicators.note: wrapping something encloses it, so the earlier words go around

blocks.clueFragment: Put Indian bread into sauce, say
blocks.note: dunking a flatbread is to dip naan, here spelt nan; say marks sauce as an example
O for old

explanation.surface: Instructions to dunk naan in a curry sauce, wrapped round an ancient fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Nan is an accepted spelling of the Indian flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipnoan is a lungfish, a primitive fish able to breathe air.

clue.text: Essential rubbish I invested in pound before sudden drop

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

blocks.note: quid is slang for a pound sterling
a dive is a plunge
tat is cheap junk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A financial tale: junk shares bought for a pound before the market plunges.
explanation.walkthrough: The rubbish and I go into the middle of the plunge, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidditative relates to quiddity, the inherent nature of a thing, so it means concerning its essence.

clue.text: Mall gallery within a month displays spotty short-haired creature

indicators.note: one thing within another sits inside it, so the gallery goes inside the month

blocks.note: the calendar abbreviation for October
the Institute of Contemporary Arts stands on The Mall in London

explanation.surface: A London gallery stages a month-long show featuring a spotted animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA (Institute of Contemporary Arts) sits on The Mall, the road leading to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocicat is a domestic cat breed with a short coat and wild-looking spots.

clue.text: Maybe area served by taxis moving east to the centre for a big fish

indicators.note: east is the compass letter, and moving it takes it from where it stood
sent to the centre means placed in the middle of the rest

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
a zone is an area, maybe the one a taxi rank covers

explanation.surface: A district covered by cabs heads east into town for a large fish dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A taxi zone is written as one word, then its final E is shifted into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabezon is a large sculpin of the North American Pacific coast, prized by anglers.

clue.text: Alternate US comedy with Calvin, Oscar and Georgia for an Asian oil producer

blocks.clueFragment: Alternate US comedy with Calvin, Oscar and Georgia
blocks.note: US comedy is HUMOR, Calvin is CAL, Oscar is O (radio alphabet), Georgia is GA (postal code); the letters of HUMOR alternate with those of CALOGA, starting with C

explanation.surface: A US sitcom stars Calvin, Oscar and a Georgia native alongside an Asian oil tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternate' is an instruction: take the letters of Calvin, Oscar and Georgia in turn with those of the comedy, starting with C.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaulmoogra is an Asian tree whose seeds yield an oil once used to treat leprosy.

clue.text: Illicitly take a pair of clubs

blocks.note: a pair is two
C for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Steal two golf clubs from the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: TWOC is British police slang from 'taken without owner's consent', used of joyriding.
explanation.definitionFit: To twoc is to steal a car for joyriding, from the legal phrase for unauthorised taking.

clue.text: Mahogany product with a carpet in wind

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it, so the pair goes inside the word for wind

blocks.note: to wind is to coil, the verb sense
taken as written
to carpet someone is to rebuke them, as is to rap

explanation.surface: Mahogany offcuts come with a carpet rolled up in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb meaning to scold, not a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Carap-oil is pressed from seeds of the carapa, a tropical tree of the mahogany family.

clue.text: Seaman cut short Latino’s greeting

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman
a razor is a cutter, with cut read as a noun phrase

explanation.surface: A sailor's chopped speech becomes a Latin American's hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish word is drawn from the verb abrazar, to hug.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrazo is the hearty embrace men exchange in Spanish-speaking countries when meeting.

clue.text: Ottoman governor’s office tones down Asian dress fullness

blocks.note: to mute is to soften
the draped garment worn in South Asia
fat as plumpness

explanation.surface: A Turkish official's bureau softens a flowing Indian robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutessarifat was the district governed by a mutessarif, an administrator in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Wrong ’un’ll mow grazed cattle’s feed plant

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, apostrophes ignored

explanation.surface: A rogue animal will chew down the pasture that cattle feed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong 'un' looks like a phrase for a villain, but Wrong is the anagram signal alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangel-wurzel is a large beet grown chiefly as winter fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Thread’s first used in mesh on a woman’s bit of hosiery — like this old one?

definitions.note: this refers back to the bit of hosiery

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone
something used in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a net is a mesh
the female possessive
the opening letter of thread
a sock is a piece of hosiery

explanation.surface: A seamstress weaves thread into a mesh stocking, wondering whether it resembles an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: The thread's initial goes inside the sock, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Netherstocks were the lower leg coverings of Tudor hose, an archaic precursor of stockings.

clue.text: She’s broken rules about what to wear in Norfolk?

blocks.note: of as in concerning
Norfolk is fen country, low marshy land in eastern England
dress is clothing

explanation.surface: A rule-breaking woman wonders about appropriate clothes in rural Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county in the flat, marshy Fens; the wordplay reads like a fashion question.
explanation.definitionFit: An offendress is an archaic word for a female offender, one who has transgressed.

clue.text: Once commanded vehement emotion, being gutted

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: hot means passionate or fierce
the first and last letters of emotion

explanation.surface: Strong feelings once ruled, though their heart has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoten is an archaic past participle of hight, meaning called or commanded.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English usage hight could mean to order, and hoten is its past form, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Annoying reversal of imperial measures about to confuse DUP’s constituency

indicators.note: a reversal reads everything that follows from the back
about means surrounding, so the measures go around the rest

blocks.note: feet are imperial units of length
to fog is to blur or confuse
the DUP, Democratic Unionist Party, stands in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Swapping back to old units muddles a Northern Irish party's voters.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb fog plus NI sits inside the measures before the whole lot is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeing off is informal for irritating or angering someone, as in 'that really tees me off'.

clue.text: Cold German greeting, something sexless, happens to show chappiness

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
the German word for hail
it is the neuter pronoun
is in the sense of exists or takes place

explanation.surface: A frosty salute and a neutral object combine to show off cheerful chumminess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chappiness' looks like a word about chaps; it means being chapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheilitis is inflammation of the lips, typically leaving them cracked and sore, i.e. chapped.

clue.text: Perhaps ironically, it’s amusing fat old slacker

blocks.note: the text-speak for laughing out loud, often typed sarcastically
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A sarcastic note that a portly old layabout is hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: Lollard was a heretic follower of Wycliffe, but an obsolete sense is an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic sense of lollard is a lazy loafer, akin to the verb loll.

clue.text: Malevolent sprite with black and dirty look

blocks.note: B for black, as on pencils
an ogle is a lecherous stare

explanation.surface: A wicked imp, dark-faced, leers at you.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogle is a goblin or spectre in Scottish and northern English folklore.

clue.text: Scrap of fish, simple to skin

indicators.note: a skin wraps what lies within, so the plain word encloses the fish

blocks.note: bare means plain, unadorned
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A morsel of fish that's easy to peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' is a fight, not a leftover.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagarre is a French loanword for a brawl or rowdy fight.

clue.text: Mouth-watering item left in salad, varying wildly

indicators.note: in places one element inside the following words
acting wildly means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: L for left
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tasty morsel abandoned in a salad of ever-changing ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth-watering' suggests delicious food; read literally, it is what makes the mouth water.
explanation.definitionFit: Salivary glands produce spit, so one is literally the organ that moistens the mouth.

clue.text: Reversible camel-hair coat

indicators.note: reversible means it reads the same either way round

blocks.note: the definition, which happens to read identically in both directions

explanation.surface: A camel-hair coat that can be worn inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a fashion description, but 'Reversible' describes the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An abba is a sleeveless Arab cloak, often woven from camel or goat hair.

clue.text: Canterbury’s remote country hog with mane similarly shorn

indicators.note: shorn means clipped, and similarly says the second word gets the same trim as the first, each losing its tail letter

blocks.note: a hog is a greedy, uncouth person, a boor
a mane is a head of hair

explanation.surface: A shaggy hog and its mane get a matching trim out in the backcountry.
explanation.walkthrough: Canterbury is the New Zealand region here, not the English city; 'similarly' says the second word is clipped too.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand slang 'up the boohai' means in the back of beyond, a remote rural district.

clue.text: Orange herbal infusion sending outsiders off facing each other

indicators.note: the outsiders are the letters at each far end, and they are sent away

blocks.note: saffron is a yellow-orange colour
a herbal tea is an infusion

explanation.surface: An orange herbal brew is pushed aside, to the drinkers face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the outermost letters of the whole phrase go: the first of the colour and the last of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Affronté is a heraldic term for two creatures depicted turned toward one another.

clue.text: Some men and woman from an earlier generation

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters

blocks.note: found across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Some men and a woman from a previous era.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is a familiar British word for a grandmother, someone a generation or two older.

clue.text: Answer Greek priestess with joke in form of self-defence

indicators.note: in places the joke inside the priestess's name

blocks.note: A for answer
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth
to kid is to joke

explanation.surface: A Greek priestess answers with a jest while practising martial arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art using throws and locks to redirect an attacker's force.

clue.text: Cadeaux from Norman and Breton location

blocks.note: et is French for and, Normandy being in France
Rennes is the capital of Brittany

explanation.surface: Gifts arrive from a Normandy town and a Brittany city.
explanation.walkthrough: The French definition hints that the answer is French too.
explanation.definitionFit: Étrennes are New Year gifts in France; cadeaux is the French word for presents.
